answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn trust-weighted access. A saffron-market contract might anchor one deposit to a persistent public key, then bridge verified payments and completed jobs to that key; counterparties can slash it for proven fraud. Spawning a thousand aliases no longer creates a thousand cheap reputations: each must tie up capital, and misconduct risks losing it. This raises the attacker’s cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or colluding validators.
